claim_summary: QuanTiMedAI contributes a feedback-driven LLM feature-selection procedure with a clinical severity channel and a modified five-VQC QLSTM predictor for cardiac-arrest mortality time series.

claim_evidence.quote: We introduce an agentic LLM-guided feature selection pipeline that iteratively refines clinical feature subsets through performance-guided feedback, incorporating clinical domain knowledge via an engineered severity score channel.
We propose a modified five-VQC QLSTM architecture with an input re-injection skip connection that improves AUROC by about 2% over a parameter-matched classical LSTM

modules.name: Outcome-guided clinical feature and severity selection
modules.scope_reason: TSK: the loop optimizes feature subsets and severity weights using mortality-prediction cross-validation feedback; changing the task family changes the objective, validation criterion, and selected features. Its temporal input summaries and feature processing are embedded in that task procedure.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - feature selection is optimized against cardiac-arrest mortality prediction performance
R4:Planning and Orchestration; Optimization and Evolution; Tools and Execution

evidence.quote: Feature selection was performed using an agentic framework driven by a large language model
Following initial selection, the feature set undergoes up to R rounds of iterative refinement.
performance feedback comprising fold-mean AUROC, AUPRC, cross-entropy loss, and per-feature permutation importance scores.

modules.name: Five-VQC QLSTM with input re-injection
modules.scope_reason: TSK: the recurrent architecture is the task-specific mortality predictor and its state transition/readout must be redesigned for a different prediction objective. It is not a general runtime or temporal data-management component.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - architecture directly implements the mortality-prediction output

evidence.quote: The proposed QuanTiMedAI replaces each classical gate with a hybrid quantum-classical block
The output-stage VQC present in the original six-VQC specification [7] is omitted, reducing the cell to five VQCs.
A residual skip connection reinjects the raw input xt directly into the hidden-refinement VQC5, preserving clinical signal that would otherwise be lost through the quantum bottleneck.

reconciliation.reason: The feature-selection mechanism is retained under the same id with current rubric labels. The packet also describes a separate architectural contribution: a five-VQC QLSTM with raw-input re-injection, which the current card omitted.

notes: The paper's LLM loop is clearly feedback-driven because inner cross-validation metrics change later feature proposals. The QLSTM is included as a separate task-specific predictor because it is a substantive architectural contribution, while the existing card omitted it.
